around.headline: Dating app trap: Bengaluru man kidnapped, robbed of Rs 3.7 lakh
around.summary: A Bengaluru man was allegedly lured to meet someone he'd been chatting with on a dating app, then kidnapped and robbed of Rs 3.7 lakh, per today's report. If you're meeting a match for the first time, insist on a public spot you choose and get there on your own.

around.headline: Hoysala patrol cops perform CPR, save scooterist's life after roadside heart attack
around.summary: Bengaluru police personnel on Hoysala patrol duty gave timely CPR to a 34-year-old scooterist who collapsed with a heart attack on a busy road, reviving him before he reached hospital, per today's reports. Dial 112 for the nearest patrol in a medical emergency, and consider learning basic CPR — it's the difference in cases like this.

around.headline: Private transport operators threaten Bengaluru bandh over bike-taxi apps
around.summary: Auto and taxi unions staged a black-flag protest and are threatening a citywide bandh if authorities don't act against bike-taxi aggregators, per today's reports. Keep an eye on this over the coming days and have a backup commute plan ready in case of a call.
around.source: The New Indian Express, The Hindu, Deccan Herald

around.headline: Auto fares rise as bike-taxi services decline in Bengaluru
around.summary: Commuters are feeling the pinch as auto fares climb alongside a drop in bike-taxi availability, per today's report. Budget a bit more for auto rides this week, and compare app fares before you book.

around.headline: Shantinagar residents ask when dug-up roads will be fixed
around.summary: Residents in Bengaluru's Shantinagar say prolonged, dust-choked road digging is dragging on with no clear end date, per today's report. If a road near you is similarly stuck mid-repair, file a complaint on the BBMP Sahaaya app to get it logged and tracked.

around.headline: Nepal flood toll climbs; hundreds of Indians still unreachable or stranded
around.summary: Nepal's flash-flood crisis continues to worsen, with roughly 320 Indians still out of contact and 400 more stranded, per today's report. If you have family or friends travelling in Nepal, check in with them and watch for state helpline updates.

street_smart.title: You match with someone on a dating app and, after a week of chatting, agree to meet for the first time. They ask you to skip the crowded cafe you suggested and instead wait at a 'quieter spot' nearby, saying they'll pick you up from there themselves — like today's case where a Bengaluru man says he was lured this way, then kidnapped and robbed of Rs 3.7 lakh. What do you do?
street_smart.based_on: Today's real incident: a Bengaluru man was allegedly kidnapped and robbed of Rs 3.7 lakh after being lured to an isolated spot through a dating-app arrangement (The Times of India). This in-person meetup safety mechanism hasn't been used as a street-smart scenario in the last three weeks — recent scam/safety topics covered BESCOM doorstep impersonation (08-29), bank-OTP calls (08-29), digital-arrest video calls (08-28), and Cognizant vishing (08-22), none about first-meetup safety.
street_smart.situation: You already like this person from your chats and don't want to seem paranoid or kill the mood by pushing back on the plan.

choices.text: Insist on sticking to the public cafe you originally suggested, get there using your own transport, and if they push back on meeting somewhere quieter or being picked up alone, treat that as a reason to cancel.
choices.feedback: Correct. A first meetup with someone you only know online should stay in a place with witnesses and easy exits, and you should control how you get there and back. Pushback on a public venue or an insistence on picking you up alone is exactly the setup used to isolate a victim before robbing or worse — the mechanism relies on removing bystanders and your own transport, not on you being naive.

choices.text: Agree to wait at the quieter spot and be picked up, since you don't want to come across as untrusting this early.
choices.feedback: This is the trap. Once you're alone with someone you've never met, in a low-visibility spot, and inside their vehicle, you've lost both witnesses and the ability to simply walk away — which is exactly how this kind of kidnap-and-rob scheme works. Politeness is not worth surrendering control of the location and your own transport.

choices.text: Go to the quieter spot as planned, but first tell a friend the person's name and dating-app profile.
choices.feedback: Telling someone who you're meeting is good practice generally, but it doesn't change what happens in the moment — you're still isolated with a stranger and inside their vehicle, with no one nearby to help if things go wrong. It only helps after the fact, not during.

choices.text: Video-call them first to confirm they look like their photos, then go ahead and meet at the quiet spot as they suggested.
choices.feedback: Confirming someone's face rules out catfishing, but it says nothing about their intentions once you're alone with them. The actual danger here is the isolated location and being picked up alone, not whether the person matches their profile picture.

takeaways: Always choose a public, populated venue yourself for a first meetup from a dating app — never let the other person redirect you to somewhere quieter.
Get to and from the first meeting using your own transport (an auto, a cab you book, your own vehicle) — never accept a pickup from someone you haven't met in person yet.
Share live location with a friend or family member for the whole meetup and agree on a check-in time; if you don't check in, that's their cue to call you or the police.

quiz.why: Police say the man was lured to an isolated spot and robbed after arranging to meet someone he'd been chatting with on a dating app.

quiz.question: Bengaluru Traffic Police this week proposed a monthly 'car-free day' aimed at which group of commuters, per today's report?
quiz.why: The proposal, aimed at easing Outer Ring Road congestion, also includes running dedicated shuttle services for tech-park employees.

quiz.question: Who announced today that they will step down as CEO of HDFC Bank?
quiz.why: Jagdishan, who took over as CEO from Aditya Puri in 2020, said he has decided not to seek reappointment.

quiz.question: Bengaluru's drinking water supply is drawn predominantly from which river, over 100 km away?
quiz.why: Water is pumped uphill from the Cauvery near Torekadanahalli, one of the largest lift-irrigation-style water supply schemes for any Indian city.

quiz.question: What is the minimum age required to contest election to the Lok Sabha in India?
quiz.why: The minimum age for the Rajya Sabha, by contrast, is 30 years.
